findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `src/rebar/metrics/__init__.py` to the edit set: import the new lens module (or call its `register()`) as a side effect, matching the existing event_metrics/git_metrics/sidecar_metrics wiring so REGISTRY hydrates for `rebar metrics`.
evidence: `src/rebar/metrics/__init__.py:18` imports `event_metrics, git_metrics, sidecar_metrics` solely for the `register()` side effect that populates REGISTRY.
`src/rebar/_commands/metrics.py:4-7` documents that importing only `rebar.metrics.registry` does NOT hydrate REGISTRY; the package `__init__` side-effect import is load-bearing.
Scope names 'src/rebar/metrics/ (new lens module + registry registration)' but does not enumerate the `__init__.py` side-effect import edit.
findings.finding: The plan omits `src/rebar/metrics/__init__.py` as a required edit target: the new lens module's `register()` only reaches `REGISTRY` (and thus `rebar metrics`) when the package `__init__` imports it for its side effect, exactly as it imports event_metrics/git_metrics/sidecar_metrics.
findings.location: Scope section — 'src/rebar/metrics/ (new lens module + registry registration)'
scenarios: A new `bug_trends.py` module defines `register()` but nothing imports it, so `rebar metrics` never surfaces the lens and AC-1 silently fails despite the module existing.
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, expand `src/rebar/metrics/` to explicitly include `__init__.py` — add the new lens module to the side-effect import list on line 18 alongside `event_metrics, git_metrics, sidecar_metrics`, and expose a `register()` that appends the spec(s) idempotently on id.

findings.finding: The plan never states whether bug_trends honors the ctx since/until range. The metrics CLI always threads a range (default last 30 days) into ctx, and existing bug/event metrics filter on it. If bug_trends respects the range, the default 30-day window excludes essentially all 344 historical closed bugs and empties the 214-bug pre-convention era-skew cohort the plan is built to surface; if it ignores the range, that deliberate deviation from every sibling metric needs to be stated.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the registry mapping: register each of the five dimensions as its own MetricSpec sharing lens='bug_trends' (the gate_economics multi-spec-per-lens pattern), so detected_by's absence yields the registry's native Unavailable per AC-3 while the others return values independently; keep only close_class's era-skew as an in-payload MISSING bucket.
evidence: registry.py evaluate() returns MetricValue OR Unavailable for the WHOLE spec; no per-dimension unavailable state
sidecar_metrics.py:282-284 registers THREE separate specs under lens='gate_economics' — the cited precedent is multi-spec-per-lens
Plan: 'a bug_trends lens with the five dimensions' vs 'detected_by degrades to unavailable without affecting others'
findings.finding: The plan does not resolve whether bug_trends is a SINGLE MetricSpec (five dimensions as keys in one value payload) or FIVE specs sharing lens='bug_trends'. The registry (evaluate/metrics_cli) returns EITHER a whole-spec MetricValue OR a whole-spec Unavailable per id and has no per-dimension unavailability facility — so AC-3 ('detected_by degrades to unavailable without affecting others') is only natively achievable if each dimension is its own spec, while AC-1's 'a bug_trends lens with the five dimensions' plus the in-payload MISSING-bucket mechanism reads as one spec. As written the two mechanisms cannot both hold under one spec.
scenarios: detected_by absent everywhere: under a single spec the lens value still computes (other dimensions), so evaluate() yields a MetricValue, not Unavailable — AC-3's 'reports unavailable' for that dimension has no registry expression and the plan defines no in-payload unavailable convention for detected_by
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt five specs (bug_close_class_by_month, bug_detected_by, bug_open_age_percentiles, bug_caused_by_fanin, bug_time_to_close) each with lens='bug_trends', source='structural', confidence='high', mirroring sidecar_metrics.register(); detected_by's compute returns None (-> Unavailable) when the field is absent everywhere, decoupling it from the other four.

findings.finding: AC-1 ('a bug_trends lens with the five dimensions') and AC-3 (detected_by degrades to unavailable 'without affecting others') cannot both be met if bug_trends is a single MetricSpec: the registry evaluates each spec atomically to ONE MetricValue or ONE Unavailable, with no notion of independently-unavailable sub-dimensions. The existing gate_economics lens registers one spec per derivation (cost_per_accepted_change / env_diagnosis_intervals / first_pass_verification) sharing lens='gate_economics'. The plan does not state whether bug_trends is one spec or five.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC-1 / AC-3; Approach ('same _spec() registration pattern')
findings.suggested_fix: Register five specs (bug_close_class_distribution, bug_detected_by_distribution, bug_open_age, bug_caused_by_fanin, bug_time_to_close) each with lens='bug_trends', so detected_by's compute returning None yields Unavailable for that spec alone.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: The five dimensions name metrics but do not state their computation/aggregation protocol: which percentiles for open-bug age and time-to-close, the timestamp fields time-to-close is derived from, and what 'caused_by fan-in per target' counts (bugs, links, distinct sources).
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Approach: 'age/time-to-close report p50/p90/p99; time-to-close = closed_at - created_at; caused_by fan-in = count of distinct caused-by bugs per target component; close_class buckets by close-month.'

findings.finding: The plan states no POSITIVE rationale for the chosen lens shape beyond 'same _spec() registration pattern as gate-economics'. Because the gate_economics precedent is actually multiple specs under one lens, the citation is ambiguous rather than a rationale, and does not justify surfacing five dimensions as one payload (if that is the intent).
scenarios: Implementer reading 'same pattern as gate-economics' would reasonably build FIVE specs (the literal precedent), contradicting a one-lens-payload reading of AC-1/AC-2

findings.finding: The plan says to 'Use the registry's source/confidence labels to flag taxonomy-window skew,' but source and confidence are CLOSED spec-level vocabularies (source∈{structural,git,sidecar,snapshot,backfill_classified}, confidence∈{high,classified}) that ride on the entire value; they cannot express a per-cohort annotation like '214 pre-convention bugs with MISSING close_class.' The skew/cohort label must be carried inside the computed value payload, not the provenance labels.
findings.location: Approach ('Use the registry's source/confidence labels to flag taxonomy-window skew')
findings.suggested_fix: Have the close_class-distribution value include a distinct 'MISSING' (pre-convention) bucket alongside the vocabulary classes, so the cohort is a labeled key in the returned distribution.
